bound_context.question: What bytes does the 217-byte leaf routine at 0x61bd410 write for a uint32_t value, and what do its callers do with the end pointer it returns?

caller_census.contract: returns dst+n, the position just past the last byte written; the callers that use it in arithmetic subtract their buffer base pointer from it to recover n
caller_census.method: Capstone disassembly of the artifact; each call site validated at the instruction boundary and attributed to the .eh_frame FDE that encloses it

claim_anchors: semantics.tsv (19 anchors: claim -> target instruction address, bytes and decoded instruction)
environment_limits: Static only: the artifact was never executed, and no source build is claimed.
The model executes the routine's decoded bytes on a small machine model that implements exactly the instructions present and raises on any other.
capstone 5.0.7 / readelf / objdump were used; results are reproducible with those tools on the digest-verified binary.
ledger: cases.tsv (300 reviewable cases, 60 per length class) with the class boundaries kept verbatim, plus nbytes and a single_32bit_store column; the full 2,400-case sweep is re-derived in memory by the tests

observations.text: Every class computes rdx = dst+n and returns it with a mov %rdx,%rax; ret pair. There are THREE such tail sites (0x61bd423, 0x61bd44e, 0x61bd4be): the 4- and 5-byte classes jmp to the first, the 1-byte class falls into it, and the 2- and 3-byte classes have their own identical copies. The returned value is a pointer, never a count.

observations.claim: five classes with inclusive unsigned bounds
observations.text: cmp/ja pairs select the class: cmp $0x7f,%esi (0x61bd417), cmp $0x3fff,%esi (0x61bd43c), cmp $0x1fffff,%esi (0x61bd460), cmp $0xfffffff,%esi (0x61bd474), each jumping away only when the value is UNSIGNED ABOVE the bound, so the bound value itself stays in the smaller class.

The 4-byte class composes the four bytes in registers (movzbl/shl $8/or at 0x61bd47c..0x61bd49d) and writes them with a single unaligned mov %ecx,(%rax) at 0x61bd4a0; the 1/2/3/5-byte classes each use one byte store per byte (0x61bd41c, 0x61bd448/44b, 0x61bd4b4..4ba, 0x61bd4ce..4e0).

observations.claim: continuation bits are or-ed in, final bytes stored unmasked
observations.text: or $0xffffff80 sets bit 7 of each non-final byte (0x61bd435, 0x61bd45a, 0x61bd46d, 0x61bd4c8); the final byte of every multi-byte class is a plain byte store, which is safe only because the class bound guarantees its value is <= 0x7f.
shr $0x1c,%esi at 0x61bd4cb puts v>>28 in the fifth byte, so for a uint32_t only its low nibble can be non-zero (0xffffffff encodes as ff ff ff ff 0f).

The body has no calls and no relocations, and every memory operand is a store; the only inputs are dst (rdi) and v (esi). The whole body is one .eh_frame FDE 0x61bd410..0x61bd4e9 (217 bytes, 62 instructions).

165 direct calls, 0 tail jumps, each validated at the instruction boundary with Capstone and attributed to the enclosing .eh_frame FDE; consumers are 139 arithmetic, 24 register-copy and 2 store, and no site discards the result.

observations.claim: the dominant caller use recovers the length
observations.text: 132 of the 139 arithmetic sites have `sub rax,<base>` as their FIRST use of the returned pointer (e.g. sub rax, r10 / sub rax, r12 / sub rax, r13 / sub rax, r14), i.e. they subtract the buffer base pointer from the end pointer to recover the encoded length; the following instructions compare that difference against a limit before storing.
Reading the routine as the LEB128 encoder for a uint32_t follows from the symbol name, the 7-bit shifts and the continuation bits; the packet does not prove the C++ level types beyond that.

observations.claim: sibling window named in the census but not covered
observations.text: The census lists GetVarint32PtrFallback (0x61bd4f0) and GetVarint64Ptr (0x61bd540) in the same coding.o; they are separate windows and are not covered here.

unknowns: The C-level types beyond the roles: the packet assumes dst is char* and v is uint32_t from the mangled signature.
Which of the 165 call sites can be reached with a value in each class at run time; the class coverage of the callers is not characterized.
The buffers' sizes at the call sites: the routine writes up to 5 bytes and performs no bound check of its own, and the callers' reservations are not verified here.
The sibling windows GetVarint32PtrFallback (0x61bd4f0) and GetVarint64Ptr (0x61bd540) are not covered.
The body is byte-identical in 3 identical source objects; only 0x61bd410 is bound.
